chapter: Church, Bel Canto and the return to music
title: Priests, Dizzy and Melba get her to Newport
summary: Priests, Dizzy and Melba Liston coaxed her out to the Newport Jazz Festival, while she was fasting.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: How did Father Crowley convince you to go back to playing?

Father Crowley and Father O'Connor talked to me, several priests. They also asked me to write a Mass, but Father Woods is the only one that really stuck with me until I really began praying, and Dizzy. Dizzy would send Melba, "Go up there and see what Lou's doing. See how she's playing." Melba, I understand, would go back and say, "Man, Lou played some chords and you ought to hear them. They're really great." He said, "Well, get her out." Melba would come here and when he took me out to the Newport Jazz Festival, Melba arranged some things. He said, "Those arrangements were really good." She said, "I didn't do them. That was Lou's arrangement. I was in the room and I just sat

down and took the music down." He said, "What! Get her out here!" He finally got me out to Newport where they were all wheeling like mad, like most of the priests did, to get me to write a Mass. Father O'Connor said, "Well, I tell you, if you don't write a Mass just play it, play it on the piano, Mass." I guess I had gotten myself so holy fasting and doing so many things and suffering, till they thought perhaps the music would be good. Sometimes I'd fast 9 days and just drink water for 9 days. The first time I fasted I ate 9 apples a day and Father Crowley came to visit me. He said, "It's a wonder you didn't turn into applesauce."
